title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
An AI-generated fake website was deployed in a cryptocurrency investment scam to deceive victims about the returns on their money. The fake site showed false investment information to a victim who believed he was using a legitimate trading platform, allowing scammers to build trust through small successful withdrawals before requesting larger investments. This is a model asserting false facts, not about the world at large but about a specific user's account and transactions.

The failure happened at the point where the victim saw information on his screen. What would have caught it: verification that the trading platform and website he accessed were genuinely operated by the company he believed was managing his money, or confirmation of his purported account through a channel he controlled independently. Whether the AI system was trained to generate convincing fake financial data, or merely used to construct the visual appearance of a legitimate site, is not established.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started when a stranger contacted Jerry Dunaway through WhatsApp. The scammer encouraged him to invest using a mobile trading app and built trust by allowing Jerry to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts of money. Over time, Jerry increased his investments, believing he was seeing legitimate returns on a real trading platform.

The scam unraveled when Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal and found he could not access his funds. Police discovered that while the trading app was genuine, scammers had created a fake website using artificial intelligence that showed false investment information on Jerry's screen. The couple lost their entire life savings and is now working with Gwinnett County police, though investigators say victims rarely recover their money in these cases. The Dunaways are speaking publicly to warn others about sophisticated scam tactics, and their children have started a GoFundMe to help with their expenses.
